problem:
Find the general solution to the problem

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-3y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-3y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -3 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda -1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =-3$ or $\lambda =1$, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{-3x}+B{e}^{x}.
$$

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is 

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)+2(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x)-3(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(2\beta -4\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(-2\alpha -4\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-4\alpha +2\beta =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ -4\beta -2\alpha =1\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{1}{2},$ $\beta =0.$

Therefore, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{-3x}+B{e}^{x}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$
